correctness.rationale: The exact Gaussian modulus identity follows from a difference-variable orthogonality sum, with radical annihilation size q/p^d; the character and frequency normalizations are explicit. The parameter-to-symmetric-matrix trace map is onto iff 1,r,r^2 are independent. The only exception is a scalar F_{p^2} subfield line, for which a relative-trace parameter gives rank zero or two and never one. Counting ranks (1,p^2-1,p^3-p^2) and annihilators yields every table entry and zero-fiber multiplicity. A self-contained packaged checker independently evaluates all frequencies and 174 complete plane classes in p=3,5 example fields, and verifies Parseval; finite checks do not replace the all-field proof.

originality.rationale: Inspection of the relevant 2026 prime-field parabola theorem and earlier finite-field Fourier uncertainty and extension manuscripts found no theorem covering the all-extension two-plane support, complete magnitude levels, exact fiber multiplicities or subfield-line minimal-zero classification. Standard quadratic Gauss orthogonality and rank counts are explicitly prior ingredients. The new component is classification and full frequency distribution of restrictions of quadratic trace forms to all additive planes. A coding-theoretic rank-enumerator equivalence remains a residual priority risk. In particular Schmidt 2018 fully covers symmetric-matrix rank counts, but not the trace-pairing family classification; a 2014 quadratic Walsh manuscript was only partially accessible.

value.rationale: An exact magnitude histogram is a natural invariant of sparse finite-field quadratic Fourier measurement systems, not a fabricated arbitrary invariant. The classification covers every two-dimensional additive support in every odd-characteristic extension degree >=3, gives the exact zero-fiber distribution, distinguishes the subfield geometry, and supplies both the optimizer classification and exact count of optimal supports. Its consequences identify a sharp subfield-induced disappearance of one amplitude level and a strict zero-count transition. Arbitrary supports or weights are outside the theorem.
